questions.solution_text:
Diagonal $AC$ splits the angles at $A$ and $C$ into two equal parts of $a^{\circ}$, and diagonal $BD$ splits the angles at $B$ and $D$ into two equal parts of $b^{\circ}$.
Each diagonal bisects the two vertex angles it passes through.

options.why: A kite need not have equal diagonals; equal diagonals are not guaranteed by the kite definition.
The axis bisects the other diagonal, but the other diagonal need not bisect the axis.

options.text: They bisect all four angles of the kite.
options.why: The axis bisects the two vertex angles it passes through. The other diagonal need not bisect the remaining angles.

The axis of a kite meets the other diagonal at a right angle.
They cross at right angles.

questions.question_text:
A quadrilateral has consecutive side lengths $6$ cm, $13$ cm, $13$ cm and $6$ cm.
What is its most appropriate name?

options.why: Treats two pairs of equal adjacent sides as four equal sides, although $6\ne13$.
Mistakes equal adjacent side pairs for equal opposite side pairs and assumes right angles that are not given.
Ignores the unequal side lengths and assumes four right angles that are not given.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the angles of a rhombus is always true?

options.text: All four angles are right angles.
options.why: Applies a square property to every rhombus, but a rhombus need not have right angles.
Would force all four angles to be equal, which only happens for a square.
Ignores that a rhombus is a parallelogram, whose opposite angles must match.

questions.solution_text:
A rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so the angles at opposite corners match.
Opposite angles are equal.

questions.question_text:
In rhombus $PQRS$, diagonal $SQ$ is drawn and $\angle PQS=28^{\circ}$.
Find $\angle SQR$.

options.why: Doubles the given half-angle to find the whole angle at $Q$, rather than its other half.
Halves the given angle again, although it is already one half of the vertex angle.
Subtracts $28^{\circ}$ from $90^{\circ}$, incorrectly assuming the rhombus has a right angle at $Q$.

questions.solution_text: $\angle SQR=28^{\circ}$, since a diagonal of a rhombus bisects the vertex angles it passes through.

questions.question_text:
The diagonals of parallelogram $ABCD$ meet at $O$, and $AO=6.3$ cm.
Find $OC$.

options.why: Doubles $AO$ to find the whole diagonal $AC$ instead of the other half $OC$.
Halves $AO$, although it is already a half-diagonal.
Misses that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so $AO=OC$.

questions.solution_text: $OC=6.3$ cm, since the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

questions.question_text:
In kite $QRST$, $QR=QT$ and $RS=ST$.
$QT=5.8$ cm, $ST=12.4$ cm and $\angle QTS=123^{\circ}$.
Which gives $QR$, $RS$ and $\angle QRS$, respectively?

options.why: Matches opposite sides instead of the stated equal adjacent side pairs.
Uses $180^{\circ}-123^{\circ}=57^{\circ}$ instead of the equal opposite-angle property of the kite.
Halves $123^{\circ}$ as though a diagonal were bisecting the requested angle; the opposite angle is equal to the whole given angle.

questions.solution_text:
$QR=5.8$ cm and $RS=12.4$ cm, since the two pairs of adjacent sides of a kite are equal.
$\angle QRS=123^{\circ}$, since the opposite angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal.

questions.question_text: Which statement about a kite is false?

options.text: A kite can have 2 right angles
options.why: Special kites can have two right angles.

options.text: A kite has diagonals which make right angles
options.why: Kite diagonals are perpendicular under the standard definition.

options.text: A kite has two pairs of equal sides
options.why: This is the defining equal-adjacent-side property.

options.text: A kite must have a pair of parallel lines

questions.solution_text: A kite need not have any parallel sides. It has two pairs of equal adjacent sides, and its diagonals are perpendicular; it can also have two right angles in a special case.
